episode_title: Season Wrap Up: Career Advice Edition

real_qa.q: What does research show about how male managers with daughters change their hiring practices for women?
real_qa.r: A study published in the Review of Economic Studies using Danish data found that after the birth of a first daughter, male managers hired women at a 2.9% higher rate and were more likely to promote women. Women working for these managers saw earnings rise by roughly 4.4%. The researchers found no drop in company performance and the women hired were just as qualified.
real_qa.requete: male managers daughters hiring women study

real_qa.q: Why did the University of Texas cut gender studies from its core curriculum?
real_qa.r: A review said that gender studies and women's studies courses were too narrow of a subject and not consistent with the idea of a core curriculum. Faculty members were asked to apply to keep their courses in the core, but only half were accepted. This followed plans to cut Latino, Black women's and gender studies as majors.
real_qa.requete: University of Texas cut gender studies core curriculum

real_qa.q: What is Valor Atomics planning to build on federal land in Utah?
real_qa.r: Valor Atomics is planning Project Beehive, a project to place hundreds of reactors on 9,000 acres of federal land held under the Bureau of Land Management in Price, Utah. The startup founder has vowed to make nuclear great again and plans to support data centers with this nuclear power infrastructure.
real_qa.requete: Valor Atomics Project Beehive Utah nuclear reactors

real_qa.q: What organizational changes is Apple's new CEO John Ternus implementing?
real_qa.r: John Ternus, a 25-year Apple veteran and longtime hardware chief who took over from Tim Cook in fall, is planning a board overhaul to sharpen Apple's engineering focus, launch products more often, and run a leaner company. Cuts have already hit program managers, including half a dozen directors and teams working on Siri, Vision Pro, and AI software.
real_qa.requete: John Ternus Apple CEO changes restructuring

real_qa.q: What violations of Department of Labor policy did Laurie Chavez Dermer face?
real_qa.r: Investigations found that Laurie Chavez Dermer had substantiated multiple violations of Department of Labor policy, including an inappropriately close and unprofessional relationship with a member of her security detail, unauthorized alcohol consumption, improperly combined Department of Labor and federal travel policy and personal travel, and created a hostile work environment at the agency.
real_qa.requete: Laurie Chavez Dermer Department of Labor violations
